meta.title: TTK-3700E PFAS-Free PPA Masterbatch | POLYTREND
meta.description: Explore TTK-3700E, a silicone-based PFAS-free PPA masterbatch for polyolefin extrusion, with film data and SGS test reports.

title: Smoother extrusion.
Without fluorine.
hero.intro: A PFAS-free polymer processing aid masterbatch in an LDPE carrier, designed to reduce die build-up and melt fracture in polyolefin extrusion.
hero.visualAlt: Illustration of pellets moving through an extruder into a smooth film
hero.visualCaption: A silicone-based route to more stable processing.

product.title: Processing efficiency. Film properties in balance.
product.intro: A processing aid should solve problems at the die—not create new ones in the film. TTK-3700E combines lubrication with measured optical and mechanical performance.

benefits.title: Control die build-up
benefits.text: Helps reduce die deposits and sharkskin in film extrusion for a smoother, more consistent surface.

benefits.title: Support efficient production
benefits.text: Lubrication helps reduce equipment wear and maintenance demands, supporting a more stable extrusion process.

benefits.title: Move beyond fluorinated PPA
benefits.text: A silicone-based, PFAS-free formulation supported by total fluorine screening and targeted PFAS analysis.

product.dosageLabel: Recommended in the performance data sheet
product.dosageTds: The TDS states a broader 0.5–5% range.
product.dosageNote: For printing or heat sealing: start at 2%, run for at least 2 hours, then adjust to the film surface.

applications.title: One material. Distinct film challenges.
applications.intro: Explore four film sectors through their process demands. Priority reflects technical fit and regulatory readiness—not certification for every end use.

hygiene.title: Breathable films for hygiene products.
hygiene.description: Highly filled PE breathable films place heavy demands on die cleanliness and thin-gauge stability. This is where PPA lubrication has a clear process role.
hygiene.note: A practical first evaluation area: no food or drug-contact claim is involved. End-product requirements still apply.

protective.title: Surface protection, down to the finish.
protective.description: For self-adhesive and coated PE films, surface defects can become marks on the protected product. Extrusion stability and gel control matter.
protective.note: Compatibility with EVA, polyisobutylene and other tackifying systems must be verified in production trials.

food.title: Flexible packaging needs a compliance-first approach.
food.description: PE sealant layers in snack, liquid, frozen-food and heavy-duty packaging face high-speed extrusion and die build-up challenges.
food.note: Important: the current TDS states that TTK-3700E is not suitable for food contact. These are industry needs, not approved end uses. Do not specify this product for food-contact packaging without a manufacturer-approved compliance basis.

medical.title: Medical packaging is a separate discipline.
medical.description: Sterile-barrier pouches and pharmaceutical packaging require controlled migration, sealing and sterilization performance.
medical.note: The TDS excludes medical implant use. External packaging is not an implant, but no medical-packaging approval is claimed here. ISO 11607, pharmacopoeia and product-specific requirements need separate verification.

performance.title: A smoother process should not compromise the film.
performance.intro: Review the data behind the product story: corona retention over 30 days and film-property comparisons at 1% addition.
performance.chartDescription: TTK-3700E at 1% and the comparison product at 3% show the same reported values: 45 initially and 40 mN/m from day 7 through day 30.
performance.resultNote: Reported for both TTK-3700E at 1% and the comparison product at 3%. Source: TDS.
performance.conditions: Source performance sheet: 30 μm blown film, 25 °C, 50% relative humidity. Test methods: GB/T 2410-08 and GB 9639-88.
performance.conclusion: Under the reported conditions, optical, mechanical, heat-seal and friction properties remain broadly comparable to untreated film. Results are formulation- and process-specific.

compliance.title: Claims are better with documents.
compliance.intro: Three SGS reports cover total fluorine screening, 671 targeted PFAS analytes and the 10 restricted RoHS substances. All were issued for the same submitted sample batch.
compliance.note: ND means not detected below the method detection limit—not absolute zero. Results apply only to the tested sample and report scope. These are test reports, not product certifications or approvals for every end market.

process.title: Start clean. Adjust to the film.
process.intro: Use the performance sheet as the starting guide, then tune to your equipment, line speed, temperature and actual film surface.

steps.title: Purge & clean
steps.text: Purge the extruder thoroughly and clean the die before introducing the masterbatch.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Mix with compatible resin at the selected ratio. Use the blend within 24 hours for best results.

steps.title: Condition the line
steps.text: When printing or heat sealing is required, start at 2% and run for at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Optimise
steps.text: Review the film surface and adjust dosage to actual process conditions. Confirm downstream performance in your own trials.

pack.label: Protect from sunlight, rain and contamination

process.note: For industrial use only. Confirm suitability for the intended formulation and end use before production.
